precepts.text: The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations; the nations were never the same, he divided them by tongue and land.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of giants; behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron”, nine cubits long and four cubits broad: about thirteen feet long and six feet wide, near the size of two king beds. That shows how tall and big this man was. To know who Og was, go to Genesis 10, where the nations are laid out: “By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.”

The Most High divided the isles of the Gentiles, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations. The nations were never the same; he divided them by tongue and by land. That is why the lineage of Og and the Amorites can be traced: each nation has its own family and its own place in Genesis 10.

precepts.text: The sons of Ham: Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan; Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations, and Kemet and Ham mean the same thing.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
“And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.” Cush is Ethiopia, Mizraim is Egypt, with Phut and Canaan. Ham, the youngest son of Noah, is the progenitor of these dark nations; Kemet and Ham mean the same thing.

This is the family Og king of Bashan comes out of. Og was an Amorite, and the Amorites come from Canaan, the son of Ham. The Hamitic nations were known for great stature: Goliath the Philistine stood nine feet nine inches, and to this day the tallest peoples on earth, the Watusi, the Dinka and the Nilotic tribes of Sudan, Ethiopia and Kenya, are Hamites. A bedstead of iron nine cubits long fits the remnant of giants that came from Ham.

precepts.text: The Jebusite and the Amorite are of the lineage of Canaan; the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, so Og the Amorite descends from Ham.
precepts.point: Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

precepts.why:
The sons of Canaan: “And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite”. The Amorite is of the lineage of Canaan, the son of Ham. So the Amorites are a Hamitic tribe, and Og king of Bashan, an Amorite and the last of the remnant of giants, descends from Ham. That lineage explains the giant, for the Hamitic nations were known for great stature.

It also explains the land. Ancient Palestine was first the land of the Philistines, Hamitic tribes, before the Arabs and later others took hold of it; the name goes back to those ancient Philistines. The land Israel took from the two kings of the Amorites, “from the river of Arnon unto mount Hermon”, all Gilead and all Bashan, was the land of the sons of Ham.

precepts.text: All the families of the Canaanites that spread abroad, begotten of Canaan.
precepts.point: They were left to prove Israel, to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments of the Most High, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Who are “all the Canaanites” the Most High left in the land to prove Israel? Genesis 10 lists the families. “And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite, And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite, And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite: and afterward were the families of the Canaanites spread abroad.”

So the Sidonians and the Hivites named among the nations that were left are themselves families of Canaan: Sidon was his firstborn, and the Hivite is one of his sons. All of these families spread abroad out of Canaan, and these are the people left in the land “to teach them war”, and to prove Israel, “to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: The Amorites go back into the Hamites: the lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan.
precepts.point: When Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent a prophet to remind them: I brought you up from Egypt out of the house of bondage, and I said, fear not the gods of the Amorites in whose land ye dwell, but ye have not obeyed my voice. The judgment came with a reason attached.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The prophet says, “fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell.” Who are the Amorites? They go back into the Hamites. “And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite.”

The lineage of the Amorites, the Jebusites, and the Perizzites all comes down from Ham through Canaan. These are the people whose land the Most High gave Israel when he “drave them out from before you”, and whose gods Israel was told not to fear. Instead, Israel did not obey his voice, and the judgment came with that reason attached.

precepts.text: The sons of Javan include Chittim, the land of Greece, so the ships come from off the coast of that European area.
precepts.point: He returns and has intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time.

note.label: Daniel 11: The Kings of the North and the South

precepts.why:
“And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.” The sons of Javan include Chittim, the land of Greece. So the ships of Chittim that come against him come from off the coast of that European area.

Grieved by them, he returns and has indignation against the holy covenant, and has intelligence with them that forsake it, because our people were forsaking the laws at this time.
